pump.homologous_form: h = H/H_R = h0*a^2 + h1*a*v + h2*v^2 ; b = T/T_R = b0*a^2 + b1*a*v + b2*v^2 ; a = N/N_R, v = Q/Q_R ; valid for a >= 0, v >= 0

check_valve.location: pump discharge, upstream of the air-vessel tee
check_valve.behaviour: ideal: closes instantly and permanently when the pump flow would reverse

profile.description: pipe centreline elevation versus chainage from the pump (P1 starts at 0, P2 at 1200, P3 at 3500, discharge at 5300); linear between points

air_vessel.location: tee at chainage 0, immediately downstream of the check valve
air_vessel.shape: vertical cylinder, internal height = 2.5 x internal diameter, bottom at elevation 100.0 m

inflow_orifice.note: differential orifice: water returning into the vessel passes the orifice; its diameter is a design choice

air_vessel.connection_loss_definition: head loss = K * Q^2 / (2 g A^2), A = area of the outflow connection (outflow) or of the inflow orifice (inflow)

event.description: pump trip at t = 0 from steady operation: motor torque drops to zero; the pump runs down under its own hydraulic torque

modelling_basis: One-dimensional elastic water hammer in each pipe with the stated wave speeds; quasi-steady Darcy friction with the stated constant friction factors; no unsteady friction.
Minor losses at pipe junctions, at the discharge and between the suction reservoir and the pump are negligible; both reservoir levels stay constant.
Initial condition: steady flow at the pump/system operating point with the motor running at rated speed.
Pump: the homologous head and torque polynomials hold for a >= 0, v >= 0; after the trip the only torque on the rotating assembly is the pump's hydraulic torque.
Check valve: ideal, as stated; once closed it stays closed.

Air vessel gas: H_abs * V_gas^n = constant, where H_abs is the absolute pressure head of the gas (gauge head + atmospheric head). The water-surface elevation in the vessel follows from the water volume and the vessel shape. Head at the tee = gas gauge head + water-surface elevation - connection loss (loss opposes the flow direction).

Pressure head along the pipeline is evaluated at the pipe centreline (profile elevation) everywhere along all three pipes over the whole simulated duration; vapour cavities and column separation are not modelled because the minimum-pressure limit is set well above vapour pressure.
The total vessel volume is the internal volume of the cylinder; the initial gas volume is the gas volume at the steady pre-trip state.
